{{lowercase}}
{{Short description|Algebra of a branch of probability theory}}
The '''σ-algebra of τ-past''', (also named '''stopped σ-algebra''', '''stopped σ-field''', or '''σ-field of τ-past''') is a [[σ-algebra]] associated with a [[stopping time]] in the theory of [[stochastic process]]es, a branch of [[probability theory]].<ref name="rajeeva47" /><ref name="klenke193" />

== Definition ==
Let <math> \tau </math> be a [[stopping time]] on the [[filtered probability space]] <math> (\Omega, \mathcal A, (\mathcal F_t)_{t \in T},  P ) </math>. Then the [[σ-algebra]]
:<math> \mathcal F_\tau:= \{ A \in \mathcal A \mid \forall t \in T \colon \{ \tau \leq t \} \cap A \in \mathcal F_t\} </math>

is called the σ-algebra of τ-past.<ref name="rajeeva47"/><ref name="klenke193"/>

== Properties ==
=== Monotonicity ===
If <math> \sigma, \tau </math> are two stopping times and
:<math> \sigma \leq \tau </math>
[[almost surely]], then
:<math> \mathcal F_\sigma \subset \mathcal F_\tau. </math>

=== Measurability ===
A stopping time <math> \tau </math> is always <math> \mathcal F_\tau</math>-[[measurable function|measurable]].

== Intuition ==

The same way <math>\mathcal{F}_t</math> is all the information up to time <math>t</math>, <math>\mathcal{F}_\tau</math> is all the information up to time <math>\tau</math>. The only difference is that <math>\tau</math> is random. For example, if you had a [[random walk]], and you wanted to ask, “How many times did the random walk hit −5 before it first hit 10?”, then letting <math>\tau</math> be the first time the random walk hit 10, <math>\mathcal{F}_\tau</math> would give you the information to answer that question.<ref name="earnest17" />
